Moving the password-driven deletes to run unconditionally before the transaction recreates the pre-#441 partial-change bug: T2's hostile fixture (a second session/push token that would survive the unfixed route) is deleted immediately, even though the subsequent role UPDATE still rolls back inside keepingAnAdmin.

label: #441: promote-admin.js's parseArgs stops stripping the `--` end-of-options marker
#441: DELETE /users/:id's keepingAnAdmin wrapper removed
note: Unreachable today, recorded honestly rather than hidden: DELETE /users/:id already refuses self-delete (checked above this wrapper), and requireAdmin re-checks the LIVE role (issue #261) on every request, while the whole handler runs synchronously with no `await`. So the caller was necessarily an admin at the exact moment this code ran, and deleting a DIFFERENT user can only reduce a count of >=2 admins, or delete a non-admin and not touch the count at all — no fixture can make this route delete the last admin without also deleting the caller's own account, which the guard above already blocks. Kept as defence in depth for if this route (or something it calls) ever grows an `await` before the deletes, which would let another request interleave.
